arguments.value:
This agreement is between the City of Fort Stockton, Texas and STW Resources Holding Corp. It gives STW the right to explore for, drill, deepen, produce, use, transport, and treat groundwater from the Capitan Reef Aquifer from specified City property, including access to the property and use of surface areas needed for pumping and filling stations. STW pays for the drilling, well work, studies, construction, insurance, and required regulatory approvals, and must repair damage and restore the surface when required.

The agreement lasts 30 years and then renews year to year unless terminated with notice. STW must first study the existing well, and if it is not suitable, STW may drill a replacement well. If the studies show the wells can produce at least 1,200 gallons per minute and the water meets the required standards, STW may choose to produce and transport the water, pay the City a $5 million bonus, owe the City a 17% royalty on water sold from the property, and provide the City up to 3 million gallons per day at no cost when requested. If the water does not meet the criterion, STW may choose not to proceed, proceed without reimbursement, or proceed if regulators approve less than requested.

The City must cooperate by providing documents, assisting with studies and approvals, and obtaining or having the necessary property rights. STW owns the wells during the agreement, but title can revert to the City if the property-related rights end and the City reimburses STW as required. The agreement also covers termination rights, reimbursement if the City later sells water from wells developed by STW, use of certain City easements and infrastructure for other Pecos County water projects, indemnity, governing law in Texas, and other standard contract terms.
